title.raw: 卷三十六 志第二十六 州郡二 Volume 36 Treatises 26: Administrative Districts 2

sentences.zh: 志第二十六 州郡二

translations.literal: Treatise 26: Administrative Districts 2
translations.idiomatic: Treatise 26: Administrative Districts, Part Two

sentences.zh: ○南豫州 豫州 江州 青州 冀州 司州

translations.literal: ○ Southern Yu Province, Yu Province, Jiang Province, Qing Province, Ji Province, Si Province
translations.idiomatic: ○ Southern Yu, Yu, Jiang, Qing, Ji, and Si Provinces

sentences.zh: 南豫州刺史，晉江左胡寇強盛，豫部殲覆，元帝永昌元年，刺史祖約始自譙城退還壽春。

translations.literal: Inspector of Southern Yu Province: during the Jin on the left bank of the Yangzi, non-Han raiders were powerful and the Yu region was overrun; in the first year of Yongchang under Emperor Yuan, Inspector Zu Yue first withdrew from Qiao city and returned to Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: Inspector of Southern Yu: When non-Han invaders were strong south of the Yangzi and the Yu region had been overrun, in Yongchang year 1 of Emperor Yuan the inspector Zu Yue withdrew from Qiao and fell back to Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 成帝咸和四年，僑立豫州，庾亮為刺史，治蕪湖。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xianhe under Emperor Cheng, Yu Province was established as a frontier administration; Yu Liang served as inspector, with his seat at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianhe year 4 of Emperor Cheng, Yu was re-established as a refugee province; Yu Liang became inspector and governed from Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 咸康四年，毛寶為刺史，治邾城。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Xiankang, Mao Bao served as inspector, with his seat at Zhucheng.
translations.idiomatic: In Xiankang year 4, Mao Bao was inspector, with his seat at Zhucheng.

sentences.zh: 六年，荊州刺史庾翼鎮武昌，領豫州。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Jing Province Inspector Yu Yi garrisoned Wuchang and concurrently held Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Jing inspector Yu Yi garrisoned Wuchang and also held Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 八年，庾懌為刺史，又鎮蕪湖。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Yu Kai served as inspector and again garrisoned Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 8, Yu Kai was inspector and again garrisoned Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 穆帝永和元年，刺史趙胤鎮牛渚。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghe under Emperor Mu, Inspector Zhao Yin garrisoned Niuzhu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghe year 1 of Emperor Mu, inspector Zhao Yin garrisoned Niuzhu.

translations.literal: In the second year, Inspector Xie Shang garrisoned Wuhu;
translations.idiomatic: In year 2, inspector Xie Shang garrisoned Wuhu;

translations.literal: in the fourth year, he advanced to Shouchun;
translations.idiomatic: in year 4 he advanced to Shouchun;

translations.literal: in the ninth year, Shang again garrisoned Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: in year 9 Shang again garrisoned Liyang;

translations.literal: in the eleventh year, he advanced to Matou.
translations.idiomatic: in year 11 he advanced to Matou.

sentences.zh: 升平元年，刺史謝奕戍譙。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shengping, Inspector Xie Yi garrisoned Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengping year 1, inspector Xie Yi garrisoned Qiao.

sentences.zh: 哀帝隆和元年，刺史袁真自譙退守壽春。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longhe under Emperor Ai, Inspector Yuan Zhen withdrew from Qiao and held Shouchun.
translations.idiomatic: In Longhe year 1 of Emperor Ai, inspector Yuan Zhen withdrew from Qiao and defended Shouchun.

sentences.zh: 簡文咸安元年，刺〔史桓熙戍歷陽。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xi'an under Emperor Jianwen, Inspect[or Huan Xi garrisoned Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xi'an year 1 of Emperor Jianwen, inspector Huan Xi garrisoned Liyang.

sentences.zh: 孝武甯康元年，刺〕史桓沖戍姑孰。

translations.literal: In the first year of Ningkang under Emperor Xiaowu, Inspect]or Huan Chong garrisoned Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: In Ningkang year 1 of Emperor Xiaowu, inspector Huan Chong garrisoned Gushu.

sentences.zh: 太元十年，刺史朱序戍馬頭。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Taixuan, Inspector Zhu Xu garrisoned Matou.
translations.idiomatic: In Taixuan year 10, inspector Zhu Xu garrisoned Matou.

sentences.zh: 十二年，刺史桓石虔戍歷陽。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, Inspector Huan Shiqian garrisoned Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12, inspector Huan Shiqian garrisoned Liyang.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙二年，刺史劉毅戍姑孰。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yixi under Emperor An, Inspector Liu Yi garrisoned Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: In Yixi year 2 of Emperor An, inspector Liu Yi garrisoned Gushu.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝欲開拓河南，綏定豫土，九年，割揚州大江以西、大雷以北，悉屬豫州，豫基址因此而立。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song wished to open up Henan and pacify the Yu territory; in the ninth year, the territory west of the great river in Yang Province and north of Dalei were all assigned to Yu Province, and the foundation of Yu was thereby established.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song sought to expand into Henan and secure the Yu region; in year 9 he assigned all of Yang west of the Yangzi and north of Dalei to Yu Province, establishing the territorial base of Yu.

sentences.zh: 十三年，刺史劉義慶鎮壽陽。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Inspector Liu Yiqing garrisoned Shouyang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 13, inspector Liu Yiqing garrisoned Shouyang.

sentences.zh: 永初三年，分淮東為南豫州，治歷陽；

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongchu, the east of the Huai was divided off as Southern Yu Province, with its seat at Liyang;
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu year 3, the Huai east was split off as Southern Yu, with its seat at Liyang;

translations.literal: the west of the Huai became Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: and the Huai west became Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉七年〔合二豫州為一，十六年又分，二十二年又合，考武大明三年〕，又分。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen [the two Yu provinces were merged into one; in the sixteenth year they were divided again; in the twenty-second year they were merged again; in the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu], they were divided again.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 7 of Emperor Wen [the two Yu provinces were united; in year 16 they were split again; in year 22 reunited; in Daming year 3 of Emperor Xiaowu], they were divided once more.

sentences.zh: 五年，割揚州之淮南、宣城又屬焉。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, Huainan and Xuancheng in Yang Province were again assigned to it.
translations.idiomatic: In year 5, Huainan and Xuancheng in Yang Province were again placed under it.

translations.literal: The provincial seat was moved to Gushu.
translations.idiomatic: The seat was moved to Gushu.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始二年又合，而以淮南、宣城還揚州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Taishi under Emperor Ming they were merged again, and Huainan and Xuancheng were returned to Yang Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 2 of Emperor Ming the provinces were merged again, and Huainan and Xuancheng were returned to Yang.

translations.literal: In the ninth month they were divided again, and the seat returned to Liyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they were split again, with the seat at Liyang.

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year, they were merged again.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of year 3 they were united again.

sentences.zh: 四年，以揚州之淮南、宣城為南豫州，治宣城，五年罷。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Huainan and Xuancheng in Yang Province were made Southern Yu Province, with its seat at Xuancheng; in the fifth year it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Huainan and Xuancheng in Yang were made Southern Yu, seated at Xuancheng; in year 5 it was abolished.

translations.literal: At that time, from the Huai westward, all had fallen to the invaders.
translations.idiomatic: By then everything west of the Huai had been lost to the invaders.

sentences.zh: 七年，復分歷陽、淮陰、南譙、南兗州之臨江立南豫州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Liyang, Huaiyin, Southern Qiao, and Linjiang in Southern Yan Province were again divided off to establish Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In year 7, Liyang, Huaiyin, Southern Qiao, and Linjiang in Southern Yan were split off again to establish Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 泰豫元年，以南汝陰度屬豫州，豫州之廬江度屬南豫州。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiyu, Southern Ruyin was transferred to Yu Province, and Lujiang in Yu Province was transferred to Southern Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taiyu year 1, Southern Ruyin was reassigned to Yu, and Lujiang in Yu was reassigned to Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 按淮東自永初至於大明，便為南豫，雖乍有離合，而分立居多。

translations.literal: Accordingly, from Yongchu down to Daming, the east of the Huai was generally Southern Yu; although there were occasional separations and reunions, separate establishment predominated.
translations.idiomatic: From Yongchu through Daming, the Huai east was generally Southern Yu; though the provinces were sometimes merged or split, they were more often separate.

sentences.zh: 爰自泰始甫失淮西，復於淮東分立兩豫。

translations.literal: From Taishi, when the west of the Huai was first lost, the two Yu provinces were again established separately on the east of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Huai west was lost at the beginning of Taishi, the two Yu provinces were re-established on the Huai east.

sentences.zh: 今南豫以淮東為境，不復於此更列二州，覽者按此以淮東為境，推尋便自得泰始兩豫分域也。

translations.literal: Now Southern Yu takes the east of the Huai as its border; the two provinces are no longer listed here separately. Readers who take the east of the Huai as the border and trace the matter will readily see how the two Yu provinces were divided in the Taishi era.
translations.idiomatic: Southern Yu now takes the Huai east as its boundary, and the two provinces are no longer listed separately here; readers who note that the Huai east is the boundary can readily infer how the two Yu provinces were divided in the Taishi period.

sentences.zh: 徐志領郡十三，縣六十一，戶三萬七千六百二，口二十一萬九千五百。

translations.literal: In the Xu-era gazetteer it governed thirteen commanderies, sixty-one counties, 37,602 households, and 219,500 persons.
translations.idiomatic: The Xu-era register lists thirteen commanderies, sixty-one counties, 37,602 households, and 219,500 people.

translations.literal: At present it governs nineteen commanderies and ninety-one counties.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs nineteen commanderies and ninety-one counties.

translations.literal: One hundred sixty li by water from the capital.
translations.idiomatic: It lies 160 li by water from the capital.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Liyang: an old Han county, subordinate to Jiujiang.
translations.idiomatic: Liyang magistrate: a former Han county belonging to Jiujiang.

sentences.zh: 烏江令，二漢無，《晉書》有烏江，《太康地志》屬准南。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Wujiang: absent in both Han dynasties; the Book of Jin has Wujiang; the Taikang Gazetteer places it under Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: Wujiang magistrate: not listed in either Han dynasty; the Book of Jin records Wujiang, and the Taikang Gazetteer assigns it to Huainan.

sentences.zh: 龍亢令，漢舊名，屬沛郡，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Longkang: an old Han name, subordinate to Pei commandery; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Longkang magistrate: an old Han name under Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

translations.literal: Established on the left bank of the Yangzi as a frontier administration.
translations.idiomatic: Established south of the Yangzi as a refugee county.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yongqiu: an old Han name, subordinate to Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Yongqiu magistrate: an old Han name under Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 流寓立，先屬泰山郡，文帝元嘉八年度。

translations.literal: Established as a frontier administration; formerly subordinate to Taishan commandery; transferred in the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Established as a refugee county; formerly under Taishan; transferred in Yuanjia year 8 of Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 酇令，漢屬沛，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Zan: under Han subordinate to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zan magistrate: under Han it belonged to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

sentences.zh: 流寓立，文帝元嘉八年度。

translations.literal: Established as a frontier administration; transferred in the eighth year of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen.
translations.idiomatic: Established as a refugee county; transferred in Yuanjia year 8 of Emperor Wen.

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Qiao: Qiao commandery is treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Qiao: see the separate entry for Qiao commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元中，於淮南僑立郡縣，後割地成實土。

translations.literal: During the Taixuan era under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, commanderies and counties were established as frontier administrations in Huainan; later territory was carved off to form actual land.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, commanderies and counties were set up as refugee administrations in Huainan; later carved-off territory became real jurisdiction.

translations.literal: The Commanderies and States also has Zan county; He and Xu do not.
translations.idiomatic: The Commanderies and States also lists Zan county, which He and Xu omit.

sentences.zh: 今領縣六，戶四千四百三十二，口二萬二千三百五十八。

translations.literal: At present it governs six counties, 4,432 households, and 22,358 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs six counties, with 4,432 households and 22,358 people.

sentences.zh: 去州水五百四十，陸一百七十；

translations.literal: Five hundred forty li by water from the province, one hundred seventy by land;
translations.idiomatic: 540 li by water and 170 by land from the provincial seat;

translations.literal: seven hundred li by water from the capital, five hundred by land.
translations.idiomatic: 700 li by water and 500 by land from the capital.

sentences.zh: 山桑令，前漢屬沛，後漢屬汝南，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shansang: under Former Han subordinate to Pei; under Later Han to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Shansang magistrate: under Former Han it belonged to Pei; under Later Han to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

sentences.zh: 譙令，漢屬沛，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Qiao: under Han subordinate to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao magistrate: under Han it belonged to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

sentences.zh: 銍令，漢屬沛，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Zhi: under Han subordinate to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi magistrate: under Han it belonged to Pei; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

sentences.zh: 扶陽令，前漢屬沛，後漢、《晉太康地志》并無。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Fuyang: under Former Han subordinate to Pei; absent in both Later Han and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Fuyang magistrate: under Former Han it belonged to Pei; it appears in neither Later Han nor the Jin Taikang Gazetteer.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Qi magistrate.

translations.literal: Treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: See separate entry.

sentences.zh: 城父令，前漢屬沛，後漢屬汝南，《晉太康地志》屬譙。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Chengfu: under Former Han subordinate to Pei; under Later Han to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: Chengfu magistrate: under Former Han it belonged to Pei; under Later Han to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Qiao.

sentences.zh: 廬江太守，漢文帝十六年，分淮南國立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Lujiang: in the sixteenth year of Emperor Wen of Han, established by dividing off from the Huainan kingdom.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Lujiang: established in year 16 of Emperor Wen of Han by splitting off from the kingdom of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 光武建武十三年，又省六安國以并焉。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Jianwu under Emperor Guangwu, the kingdom of Lu'an was again abolished and merged into it.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 13 of Emperor Guangwu, the kingdom of Lu'an was abolished and merged into it.

sentences.zh: 領縣三，戶一千九百九，口一萬一千九百九十七。

translations.literal: It governs three counties, 1,909 households, and 11,997 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It governs three counties, with 1,909 households and 11,997 people.

sentences.zh: 去州水二千七百二十，陸四百七十；

translations.literal: Two thousand seven hundred twenty li by water from the province, four hundred seventy by land;
translations.idiomatic: 2,720 li by water and 470 by land from the provincial seat;

sentences.zh: 去京都水一千一百，陸六百三十一。

translations.literal: one thousand one hundred li by water from the capital, six hundred thirty-one by land.
translations.idiomatic: 1,100 li by water and 631 by land from the capital.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Qian: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Qian magistrate: a former Han county.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shu: an old Han county.
translations.idiomatic: Shu magistrate: a former Han county.

sentences.zh: 始新令，《永初郡國》、何並無，徐有始新左縣，明帝泰始三年立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shixin: absent in the Yongchu Commanderies and States and in He; Xu has Shixin Left county; established in the third year of Taishi under Emperor Ming.
translations.idiomatic: Shixin magistrate: omitted in the Yongchu Commanderies and States and in He; Xu lists Shixin Left county; established in Taishi year 3 of Emperor Ming.

sentences.zh: 南汝陰太守汝陰郡別見，江左立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Ruyin: Ruyin commandery is treated separately elsewhere; established on the left bank of the Yangzi.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Ruyin: see the separate entry for Ruyin commandery; established south of the Yangzi.

sentences.zh: 領縣五，戶二千七百一，口一萬九千五百八十五。

translations.literal: It governs five counties, 2,701 households, and 19,585 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It governs five counties, with 2,701 households and 19,585 people.

translations.literal: Three hundred li by land from the province;
translations.idiomatic: 300 li by land from the provincial seat;

sentences.zh: 去京都水一千，陸五百三十。

translations.literal: one thousand li by water from the capital, five hundred thirty by land.
translations.idiomatic: 1,000 li by water and 530 by land from the capital.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Ruyin: treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Ruyin magistrate: see separate entry.

sentences.zh: 所治即二漢、晉合肥縣，後省。

translations.literal: Its seat of government was the Hefei county of both Han dynasties and Jin; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Its seat was the Hefei county of both Han dynasties and Jin; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 慎令，漢屬汝南，《晉太康地志》屬汝陰。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Shen: under Han subordinate to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Ruyin.
translations.idiomatic: Shen magistrate: under Han it belonged to Runan; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Ruyin.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Song magistrate.

translations.literal: Treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: See separate entry.

sentences.zh: 陽夏令，前漢屬淮陽，後漢屬陳。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yangxia: under Former Han subordinate to Huaiyang; under Later Han to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yangxia magistrate: under Former Han it belonged to Huaiyang; under Later Han to Chen.

sentences.zh: 《晉太康地志》陳令屬梁，無復此縣。

translations.literal: The Jin Taikang Gazetteer places the Chen magistrate under Liang; this county no longer exists.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Taikang Gazetteer assigns Chen to Liang; the county no longer appears.

sentences.zh: 又晉地志，惠帝永康中復立。

translations.literal: Again, in the Jin Gazetteer, it was re-established in the Yongkang era under Emperor Hui.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin Gazetteer also records that it was re-established in the Yongkang era of Emperor Hui.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》、何并屬南梁，徐志屬此。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He both place it under Southern Liang; the Xu-era gazetteer places it here.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He assign it to Southern Liang; the Xu-era register places it here.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Anyang: treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Anyang magistrate: see separate entry.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》、何并屬南梁，徐屬此。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He both place it under Southern Liang; Xu places it here.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He assign it to Southern Liang; Xu places it here.

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Liang: Liang commandery is treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Liang: see the separate entry for Liang commandery.

sentences.zh: 晉孝武太元中，僑立于淮南，安帝始有淮南故地，屬徐州。

translations.literal: During the Taixuan era under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin, it was established as a frontier administration in Huainan; under Emperor An the old Huainan territory was first obtained and it was subordinate to Xu Province.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taixuan era of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin it was set up as a refugee administration in Huainan; under Emperor An the old Huainan lands were recovered and it belonged to Xu Province.

sentences.zh: 武帝永初二年，還南豫，孝武大明六年廢屬西豫，改名淮南，八年復舊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongchu under Emperor Wu it returned to Southern Yu; in the sixth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu it was abolished and assigned to Western Yu, renamed Huainan, and in the eighth year restored to the former name.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongchu year 2 of Emperor Wu it returned to Southern Yu; in Daming year 6 of Emperor Xiaowu it was abolished and assigned to Western Yu, renamed Huainan, and in year 8 restored to its former name.

sentences.zh: 《永初郡國》又有虞、陽夏、安豐三縣。

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also has Yu, Yangxia, and Anfeng counties.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States also lists Yu, Yangxia, and Anfeng counties.

translations.literal: All are treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: All are covered in separate entries.

translations.literal: He and Xu lack Anfeng;
translations.idiomatic: He and Xu omit Anfeng;

sentences.zh: 又有義昌而并無寧陵縣。

translations.literal: there is also Yichang, and together they lack Ningling county.
translations.idiomatic: and list Yichang while omitting Ningling county.

sentences.zh: 今領縣九，戶六千二百一十二，口四萬二千七百五十四。

translations.literal: At present it governs nine counties, 6,212 households, and 42,754 persons.
translations.idiomatic: It now governs nine counties, with 6,212 households and 42,754 people.

sentences.zh: 去州水一千八百，陸五百；

translations.literal: One thousand eight hundred li by water from the province, five hundred by land;
translations.idiomatic: 1,800 li by water and 500 by land from the provincial seat;

sentences.zh: 去京都水一千七百，陸七百。

translations.literal: one thousand seven hundred li by water from the capital, seven hundred by land.
translations.idiomatic: 1,700 li by water and 700 by land from the capital.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Suiyang: an old Han name.
translations.idiomatic: Suiyang magistrate: a former Han name.

translations.literal: Together sixteen counties and 1,992 households.
translations.idiomatic: Together sixteen counties and 1,992 households.

sentences.zh: 少帝景平初，司州複沒北虜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, Si Province again fell to the northern barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jingping under the Lesser Emperor, Si Province again fell to the northern enemy.

sentences.zh: 文帝元嘉末，僑立于汝南，尋亦省廢。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen, it was established as a frontier administration in Runan, but soon abolished again.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia under Emperor Wen it was set up as a refugee administration in Runan, but was soon abolished again.

sentences.zh: 明帝複于南豫州之義陽郡立司州，漸成實土焉。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming again established Si Province in Yiyang commandery of Southern Yu Province, gradually becoming actual territory.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming re-established Si Province in Yiyang commandery of Southern Yu Province, and it gradually became real territory.

sentences.zh: 領郡四，縣二十，去京都水二千七百，陸一千七百。

translations.literal: It governed four commanderies and twenty counties, 2,700 li by water from the capital and 1,700 by land.
translations.idiomatic: It governed four commanderies and twenty counties, 2,700 li by water and 1,700 by land from the capital.

sentences.zh: 義陽太守，魏文帝立，後省，晉武帝又立。

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Yiyang: established under Emperor Wen of Wei; later abolished; re-established under Emperor Wu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Yiyang: established under Emperor Wen of Wei; later abolished; re-established under Emperor Wu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 《太康地志》、《永初郡國》、何志並屬荊州，徐則南豫也。

translations.literal: The Taikang Gazetteer, the Yongchu Commanderies and States, and He's gazetteer all place it under Jing Province; the Xu-era register places it under Southern Yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Taikang Gazetteer, the Yongchu Commanderies and States, and He's register all assign it to Jing Province; the Xu-era register assigns it to Southern Yu.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始五年，度郢州，後廢帝元徽四年，屬司州。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Taishi under Emperor Ming it was transferred to E Province; in the fourth year of Yuanhui under the Deposed Emperor it was subordinate to Si Province.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 5 of Emperor Ming it was transferred to E Province; in Yuanhui year 4 of the Deposed Emperor it belonged to Si Province.

translations.literal: It governs seven counties.
translations.idiomatic: It governs seven counties.

sentences.zh: 戶八千三十二，口四萬一千五百九十七。

translations.literal: 8,032 households and 41,597 persons.
translations.idiomatic: 8,032 households and 41,597 people.

sentences.zh: 平陽侯相，前漢無，後漢屬江夏曰平春，《晉太康地志》屬義陽，晉孝武改。

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Marquisate of Pingyang: absent under Former Han; under Later Han subordinate to Jiangxia as Pingchun; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang; changed under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the Marquisate of Pingyang: not in Former Han; under Later Han it belonged to Jiangxia as Pingchun; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang; renamed under Emperor Xiaowu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 鄳令，二漢屬江夏，《晉太康地志》屬義陽，並作鄳，音盲。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Meng: under both Han dynasties subordinate to Jiangxia; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang; all write it as Meng, pronounced meng.
translations.idiomatic: Meng magistrate: under both Han dynasties it belonged to Jiangxia; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang; all sources write it as Meng, pronounced meng.

translations.literal: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He both write it as Meng.
translations.idiomatic: The Yongchu Commanderies and States and He both write it as Meng.

sentences.zh: 鐘武令，前漢屬江夏，後漢、《晉太康地志》無，《永初郡國》屬義陽。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Zhongwu: under Former Han subordinate to Jiangxia; absent under Later Han and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer; the Yongchu Commanderies and States place it under Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongwu magistrate: under Former Han it belonged to Jiangxia; omitted under Later Han and the Jin Taikang Gazetteer; the Yongchu Commanderies and States place it under Yiyang.

sentences.zh: 寶城令，孝武孝建三年，分鄳立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Baocheng: in the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, established by splitting off from Meng.
translations.idiomatic: Baocheng magistrate: established in Xiaojian year 3 of Emperor Xiaowu by splitting off from Meng.

sentences.zh: 義陽令，《晉太康地志》有，後省。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Yiyang: present in the Jin Taikang Gazetteer; later abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Yiyang magistrate: listed in the Jin Taikang Gazetteer; later abolished.

sentences.zh: 孝武孝建三年，分平陽立。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, established by splitting off from Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Established in Xiaojian year 3 of Emperor Xiaowu by splitting off from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 平春令，孝武孝建三年，分平陽立。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Pingchun: in the third year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu, established by splitting off from Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Pingchun magistrate: established in Xiaojian year 3 of Emperor Xiaowu by splitting off from Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 環水長，《永初郡國》、何、徐並無。

translations.literal: Chief of Huanshui: absent in the Yongchu Commanderies and States, He, and Xu.
translations.idiomatic: Huanshui chief: omitted in the Yongchu Commanderies and States, He, and Xu.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始三年，度屬宋安郡，後省宋安，還此。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi under Emperor Ming it was transferred to Song'an commandery; later Song'an was abolished and it returned here.
translations.idiomatic: In Taishi year 3 of Emperor Ming it was reassigned to Song'an; after Song'an was abolished it returned here.

sentences.zh: 宋安，本縣名，孝武大明八年，省義陽郡所統東隨二左郡立為宋安縣，屬義陽。

translations.literal: Song'an, originally a county name: in the eighth year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu, the two left-bank commanderies of Eastern Sui under Yiyang commandery were abolished and established as Song'an county, subordinate to Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Song'an, originally a county name: in Daming year 8 of Emperor Xiaowu, the two Eastern Sui left commanderies under Yiyang were abolished and made Song'an county under Yiyang.

translations.literal: Emperor Ming established it as a commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming made it a commandery.

sentences.zh: 隨陽子相，漢隨縣屬南陽，《晉太康地志》屬義陽。

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Viscountate of Suiyang: under Han Sui county belonged to Nanyang; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the Viscountate of Suiyang: under Han, Sui county belonged to Nanyang; the Jin Taikang Gazetteer places it under Yiyang.

translations.literal: Later both the Sui state and the commandery were renamed.
translations.idiomatic: Later both the Sui state and the commandery were renamed.

translations.literal: Chancellor of the Barony of Yongyang: present in the Xu-era gazetteer.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor of the Barony of Yongyang: listed in the Xu-era register.

sentences.zh: 關西令別見荊州，作厥西。

translations.literal: Magistrate of Guanxi: treated separately under Jing Province; written as Juexi.
translations.idiomatic: Guanxi magistrate: see Jing Province; written as Juexi.

translations.literal: Newly established at the end of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Newly established late in Song.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Xipinglin: newly established at the end of Song.
translations.idiomatic: Xipinglin magistrate: newly established late in Song.

translations.literal: Grand Administrator of Southern Runan.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrator of Southern Runan.

translations.literal: Runan commandery: treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Runan commandery: see separate entry.

translations.idiomatic: Pingyu magistrate.

translations.idiomatic: Northern Xinxi magistrate.

translations.idiomatic: Zhenyang magistrate.

translations.idiomatic: Ancheng magistrate.

translations.idiomatic: Southern Xinxi magistrate.

translations.literal: Magistrate of Anyang.
translations.idiomatic: Anyang magistrate.

translations.literal: All are treated separately elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: All are covered in separate entries.

translations.idiomatic: Linru magistrate: newly established.
